_doc: How a place is BUILT on the ground. The complaint was that a landmark was 'a couple of random models thrown on top of a coordinate location' — so nothing here is one model. A layout is an approach you walk up, a centre you can see from the next ridge, and surroundings that say who used to be here. js/sites.js owns the geometry for each `piece`; this file owns where the pieces go, so a new place is a few lines of JSON and no new code. Distances are metres, angles are TURNS (0..1, so 0.25 is a quarter way round). Original names and ideas only.
_ringDoc: A ring of N pieces at radius R only closes if N is at least 2*pi*R divided by the piece's width (a palisade is 6 m, a curtain wall 9 m) times its scale. Below that you get a picket fence with the middle missing, which is what the first pass shipped. `skip` is then what makes a gate a gate. A ring that is MEANT to be a ruin — a burnt farm, a hunting blind, an abandoned tower — says `broken: true` and is left alone.

_schema.tall: roughly how high the tallest piece stands — used by the tests to check a set piece is actually visible from a distance
_schema.centre: [{ piece, scale, x, z, y, spin }] — the thing you came to see
_schema.rings: [{ piece, count, radius, scale, rotate: in|out|tangent|random, offset (turns), angle (turns, for a single piece), skip: [index], jitter, y }]
_schema.approach: { piece, count, from, to, spread, scale, both } — markers that walk you in from `from` metres out to `to` metres out. `both` puts a line either side, which is what makes it read as an avenue rather than a trail of litter
_schema.scatter: [{ piece, count, radius, scale, inner }] — what is lying about
_schema.fires: [{ r, a }] — a lit brazier at radius r, angle a. These become real lights.
_schema.hostile: true if the layout belongs to something that will fight you (used by the POI test)

_worldBossDoc: The four world-boss arenas used by data/worldbosses.json — boss_bonefield, boss_barrow, boss_slagpit, boss_ironmuster. They are built WIDE on purpose: the thing standing in the middle is six to nine metres tall and keeps calling bodies up, so the ring has to be somewhere you can actually back off inside. No new geometry — all four are composed out of the same nineteen pieces the strongholds already use.
_instanceDoc: The twenty `inst_*` layouts are the MOUTHS of data/instances.json — what an instance looks like from outside, before you press E. Each one has to read as what it is from the next ridge: a cave is a den with rubble and bones round it, a fallow farmstead is a hut with its fence gone to stakes, a barrow is a mound with its doorstone lying flat, and the dragon's lair is a den at more than twice scale with bones in a ring and fires still lit. `tall` on every one of them is COMPUTED from the tallest piece it places times that piece's scale, not guessed — the gibbet above says 9 for a 6.16 m cage, and a set piece that lies about its height is culled at the wrong distance.

cairn_field._r14: The blurb promises 'thirty piles of stone, laid out in rows by somebody careful' and this used to be two rings of `rubble` — a 1.8 m heap of broken stone. Thirty real `cairn` pieces (3.4 m, stacked, solid) in a 6x5 grid with three gaps where somebody was never buried, the menhir still standing over them, and the waystone avenue walking you in.

boss_bonefield._centreDoc: The middle is EMPTY, and that is the rule for all four of these: js/sites.js spawns the boss at the site's own coordinate, so a centre piece there puts a nine-metre body inside a solid model — found in a screenshot, where the den completely hid the thing it was the den of. The structure sits behind the clearing instead, which also reads better: you come up the avenue, the boss is standing in the open, and its lair is at its back.

warcamp_sootwick._r27: R27 M10 — the Sootwick Gang's junk wall.

warcamp_ashtusk._r27: R27 M10 — the Ashtusk Horde's palisade (M3's orc wall) with bone totems.

warcamp_thornmane._r27: R27 M10 — the Thornmane ring of cut thorn, hide tents inside.

warcamp_unburied._r27: R27 M10 — the Unburied barrow-fort: an opened barrow ringed by earth banks and M3's bone wall at the gate.

warcamp_stonehide._r27: R27 M10 — the Stonehide ring of standing slabs round the clan fire.
